property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: AbsFwdOp/autotune_2d (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/autotune/abs/abs_2d.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 2/2 (max_rel 0.0 -- abs is exact). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

(R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: AdaLayerNormZeroFwdOp/high_perf (intent=example, kernel=examples/norm/ada_layer_norm_and_zero.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 1/5. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 3/3. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: EluFwdOp/npuir_active (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/npuir/active_ops/test_elu.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 3/3. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: EluFwdOp/npuir_active (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/npuir/active_ops/test_elu.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 3/3. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 4/4. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 4/4. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 4/4. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

(R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/2 (the one NN case; 11 trans_b cases refused). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: 🚨 R282 G1 FAIL 0/2 -- max_abs 0.00390625 vs atol=1e-3, guards clean: 2 float16 ulps from a different rounding order. A numerical-contract miss, NOT a defect. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: ops-nn: ops-nn's aclnnLayerNorm dispatches to the compiled LayerNormV4 kernel only for bfloat16 with a reduce axis of 1024 or 4096 on ascend910b (IsV4SocCheck in norm/layer_norm_v4/op_host/op_api/aclnn_layer_norm.cpp); for float16/D=8192 it runs CANN's built-in LayerNormV3, which this package does not contain (strace: R251-data/logs/tier-check-layernorm-shapes.log). Reporting that as a handwritten baseline would be the PROJECT_STATE 13.90 fallback; tilelang-mlir-ascend: LayerNormFwdOp/high_perf (intent=example, kernel=examples/norm/layer_norm.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R278 G1 PASS 2/5. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 2/2. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 1/3 -- same fp16 rotation limit. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: SeluFwdOp/npuir_active (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/npuir/active_ops/test_selu.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 2/2. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: SeluFwdOp/npuir_active (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/npuir/active_ops/test_selu.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 2/2. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.value: tilelang-mlir-ascend: SeluFwdOp/npuir_active (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/npuir/active_ops/test_selu.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 2/2. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: 🚨 R282 G1 FAIL 0/1 -- max_abs 0.015625 vs atol=1e-3, guards clean: their whole chain is fp16, our golden has an fp32 intermediate. A numerical-contract miss, NOT a defect. TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.name: baseline_refused
property.value: tilelang-ascend: block_M=4 with VEC_NUM=2 gives 2 lane(s) in this kernel's per-row statistic buffer, below the measured floor of 8: an Ascend vector instruction addresses whole 32-byte blocks, so a shorter operand encodes a zero-block repeat and the core raises `aicore exception 507015 ... fftsplus aivector error`. Measured for examples/softmax/example_online_softmax.py::online_softmax in docs/reports/R337-data/probe/online-softmax-sweep/summary.tsv (lanes 1/2/4 fault, lanes 8 correct); the same constant our own kernels carry as ROW_EXTENT_GRAIN=8 (R200). Re-fitting it would need the statistics padded to 8 lanes independently of how many rows a lane owns -- a change to the example, not a tile choice (G4); tilelang-mlir-ascend: SoftmaxFwdOp/autotune_2d (intent=unit_test, kernel=testing/autotune/softmax/softmax_2d.py): tilelang-mlir-ascend cannot be raced in-process: its Python package is also called `tilelang` and its build/libtilelang.so shares our soname, so importing it here would either shadow or collide with the tilelang that compiled the tested side (D042/R272 -- STB_GNU_UNIQUE, and neither RTLD_LOCAL nor DEEPBIND gets out of it). Handing _race a placeholder callable is not an alternative, and T289 measured what actually happens rather than predicting it: the D032 timer REFUSES a block that emits no device kernel (devicetimer.py:344, 'produced no device kernel'), and because _race puts every candidate in ONE session, that exception takes the whole selection session down -- the other candidates lose their measurement too. (R278 section 6.1 predicted a ~0 us candidate being elected as infinitely fast; the direction was right, the mechanism was not -- the timer's guard fires first. R289-data/02-counterfactual.json.) This baseline is measured out of process by baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case(); see docs/reports/R278.md. MEASURED ELSEWHERE, NOT MISSING: docs/reports/R282-data/22-timing-summary.json (34 cases x N=5 cross-process, D032 timer, bias band 3.2051%) and docs/reports/R278-data/07-summary.json (26 cases x N=5); the driver is docs/reports/R282-data/scripts/time282.py, which calls baselines._b_tl_mlir.measure_case() directly. This entry's own gate verdict is: R282 G1 PASS 1/1 (max_rel 2.70e-7; fp32 2-D case only -- the 3-D cases reduce dim=0, see R282 B4). TO PUT IT IN THE POOL, adapters/handwritten.py would need a candidate that carries a device_us measured in another process; today _race() times every candidate itself in the caller's session (adapters/handwritten.py:215-247) and there is no channel for a pre-measured one. See R289.md divergence 1.

property.value: ops-transformer-b1: TopkSelectorFwdOp is a masked top-k over a [B, S, Skv, G] fp32 score with a per-row [starts, ends) window, Skv = 65536 and topk = 1024/2048. All three candidates are eliminated by measurement (R253-data/indexing-candidates.json, R253-data/topk-manifest-shape.json): (1) aclnnMoeGatingTopK (tr_b2) -- last axis hard-limited to 2048: 2048 ok, 2049 returns 561002; (2) aclnnMoeGatingTopKSoftmax (tr_b1) -- reaches 65536, but it FUSES the normalization: for x=[3,1,2,0] it returns [0.6439, 0.2369], which is softmax(x) at indices 0 and 2, not the raw scores; our operator is handed an already-computed score and must not renormalize. It also has no mask/start/end input, so the [starts, ends) window -- the whole point of the operator -- cannot be expressed, and k = 2048 returns 561002 at Skv = 65536 (k = 1024 is the ceiling); (3) ops-math radix_top_k -- listed among the 41 ops with an ascend910b config, but it has no op_host/op_api directory at all, so it exports no aclnn entry point (ops-math's libcust_opapi.so exports 8 aclnn symbols, none of them top-k), and it is not among the 9 operators built into opp_math_b3. It would need both a new build and a new API layer. coverage_status = public_handwritten_gap

It also has no mask/start/end input, so the [starts, ends) window -- the whole point of the operator -- cannot be expressed, and k = 2048 returns 561002 at Skv = 65536 (k = 1024 is the ceiling); (3) ops-math radix_top_k -- listed among the 41 ops with an ascend910b config, but it has no op_host/op_api directory at all, so it exports no aclnn entry point (ops-math's libcust_opapi.so exports 8 aclnn symbols, none of them top-k), and it is not among the 9 operators built into opp_math_b3. It would need both a new build and a new API layer. coverage_status = public_handwritten_gap
